content.title: Cricket is thriving in Seattle along with the game’s energy, drama and quirks | The Seattle Times
content.text: Skip Ad Skip to content Skip Ad Tehmosp Khan, a member of the Seattle Aviators, demonstrates bowling at Magnuson Park in Seattle. The Aviators are part of Seattle Cricket Club, a sports club with dozens of teams across the Pacific Northwest. (Nick Wagner / The Seattle Times) Skip Ad By Christopher Sandford Special to The Seattle Times IMAGINE YOU’RE IN THE MIDDLE of a hushed stadium facing an elite pitcher who’s preparing to hurl the ball at you at high speed from about 65 feet. You’re armed with a 3-foot-long, paddle-shaped wooden club, and a pair of protective pads wrapped around your legs. Your only other weapon is your nerve.The pitcher dashes headlong from the outfield to the mound, then propels a cherry-red leather ball in the general direction of your ankles. If you’re lucky, the ball will hit the turf in front of you, deviate sharply left or right, and then rear up like a skipping rock somewhere toward your midriff. Less lucky and the pitcher will drop the ball in shorter, so it bounces off the grass and bears in on your head. (The prudent batter will also be wearing a helmet.)
